title: Mshta command references a remote resource
description: Detects mshta command lines referencing HTTP, HTTPS or FTP resources, including inline script download expressions. Process creation alone does not prove retrieval or execution.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may use mshta to retrieve and execute remotely hosted script or HTA content.
hypothesis.rationale: Remote content passed to the Windows-signed mshta binary is a recognized proxy-execution pattern that can bypass normal application expectations, although some legacy applications and administrative workflows may use remote HTA resources.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify mshta processes whose command line references a remote HTTP, HTTPS or FTP resource while leaving local HTA execution and unrelated processes unmatched.

data_sources.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint process events

triage.summary: Validate the remote resource, originating process and user intent, then inspect the process tree and network activity for follow-on execution.
steps: Review the complete mshta command line, parent process, remote URL, file path, initiating account and device context.
Determine whether the URL and HTA workflow belong to an approved legacy application, installer or administrative process.
Inspect child processes, downloaded files, script execution and network connections; isolate the device if the remote content is untrusted or unexplained.
false_positives: Approved legacy applications, installers and administrative workflows that launch a remote HTA resource

validation.expected_outcome: Match mshta command lines containing HTTP, HTTPS or FTP resources; do not match local HTA files, other processes or incomplete events.

limitations: This single-event signal does not establish malicious intent or successful execution. Renamed binaries, alternate tools, obfuscation and unlogged activity can evade the bounded predicates.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
